Explain how a VPN works in simple words
8:44 AM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and everything you send goes through it scrambled.

Without a VPN, your internet provider and the Wi-Fi owner can see which sites you visit, and sites see your real address. With one, your traffic is locked before it leaves your device, travels through the tunnel to the VPN company's computer, and only then reaches the website. The site sees the VPN's address, not yours.

It's useful on public Wi-Fi or to hide your browsing from your provider. It doesn't make you anonymous, though, because the VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
